name: Deep Dive — Endpoint
description: BEFORE RUNNING: {{TARGET}} is auto-filled when you send an asset from the Assets list; otherwise replace it. Also fill the test-account placeholders below. Authenticated, single-endpoint deep test of {{TARGET}} — strictly in-scope to it. Test-account context: [account A session/token], and for IDOR, [account B id/session]. Strictly in-scope. Read-only by default — perform a state-changing request only if the program's rules of engagement explicitly permit it, and only against your own test objects. goal: Determine whether {{TARGET}} enforces proper authentication, authorization/ownership, and input validation. Systematically test: (1) access with no credentials and with a stripped/forged token; (2) IDOR/BOLA — access account B's object while authenticated as account A, and vice versa; (3) token and JWT handling (alg confusion, weak/absent signature, replay, scope escalation); (4) parameter tampering, injection, and mass-assignment on every parameter; (5) business-logic and rate-limit abuse. Deliver only findings you actually reproduced, each in scope, with the exact request, the exact response proving impact, and a minimal PoC. If nothing reproduces, report that the endpoint resisted the tests — do not pad with unverified or theoretical issues.

name: Deep Dive - SSRF
description: Server-Side Request Forgery: find URL-fetching features and reach internal/metadata services. Replace {{TARGET}}.
goal:
Deep dive for Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) on {{TARGET}}. Find every feature that makes the server fetch a URL/host on your behalf: webhooks, image/avatar/URL proxies, link-preview/unfurl, PDF/screenshot/thumbnail generators, import-from-URL, file-from-URL, SSO/OIDC metadata or JWKS URLs, XML/SVG parsers, and any param holding url/uri/callback/dest/host/domain. For each, test pointing it at: an attacker-controlled host (confirm outbound via OOB/collaborator); internal addresses (127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254 + cloud metadata, 10./172.16./192.168., .internal/.local, link-local); alternate schemes (file://, gopher://, dict://); and redirect/parser-confusion bypasses of any allow-list. Prove impact: read cloud metadata/credentials, reach an internal service, or confirm blind SSRF out-of-band. Distinguish full-response from blind SSRF.

name: Deep Dive - Subdomain Takeover
description: Dangling-DNS subdomain takeover via deprovisioned third-party services. Replace {{TARGET}}.
goal:
Deep dive for subdomain takeover on {{TARGET}} and its in-scope subdomains. For each host, resolve the DNS chain (CNAME/A) and identify dangling pointers to third-party services that are deprovisioned/unclaimed: S3/CloudFront, GitHub Pages, Heroku, Azure, Fastly, Shopify, Zendesk, Netlify, Vercel, Surge, Readme, Helpscout, etc. A takeover exists when the host points at a provider resource returning the provider's no-such-bucket/app/site fingerprint AND the resource is claimable. Confirm the fingerprint from the live HTTP response; do NOT actually claim the resource - describe the claimable state as proof. Also flag NS-delegation takeovers. Impact: full control of a subdomain's content.

name: Deep Dive - Auth & JWT
description: Auth/JWT/session flaws: alg confusion, weak secrets, reset/OTP, fixation. Replace {{TARGET}}.
goal:
Deep dive for authentication and session weaknesses on {{TARGET}}. If JWTs are used: test alg=none, algorithm confusion (RS256 to HS256 using the public key as the HMAC secret), weak/guessable HMAC secret, unverified signature, kid path-traversal/SQLi, and expired/replayed tokens. Test session management: fixation, missing invalidation on logout/password-change, predictable tokens, missing Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite. Test auth flows: password-reset token entropy/leakage/reuse, OTP/2FA brute-force or bypass, account enumeration. Prove each with the actual request/response (a forged token accepted, a reset token reused). Use ONLY your own test accounts; never touch real users.
